problem: Kaibel Problem 1, OWR 50/2018 printed pages 3014–3015, PDF pages 46–47

quantifiers.graph: One undirected graph G=(V,E). Feasibility requires a spanning tree, so hardness may restrict to connected simple graphs.
quantifiers.arc_set: Exactly both directed versions of each undirected edge: A has 2|E| arcs.
quantifiers.root_set: Every vertex r in V, including any vertices introduced by a reduction.
quantifiers.costs: One entire arbitrary cost vector c_r in R^A for each root; no root independence, symmetry, separability, or nonnegative-cost restriction imposed by source.
quantifiers.solution: One common undirected spanning tree T⊆E. Each T^r is uniquely induced by T and the root r; roots do not choose independent arborescences.
quantifiers.objective: minimize sum over all r in V of c_r(T^r), where c_r(T^r) sums that root’s coefficients on all N−1 directed arcs of T^r.

orientation_note: The source calls T^r an arborescence rooted at r without explicitly spelling out outward or inward. A proof may fix outward orientation; transposing every root’s arc coefficients proves the identical hardness for inward convention.
encoding_note: The source uses R-valued vectors without a bit model. A finite binary/unary nonnegative-integer subclass suffices for NP-hardness; NP membership must be stated for finitely encoded coefficients, not arbitrary real inputs.
distinct_problem2: Directed graph, one fixed root, destination-specific costs on root-to-destination paths; distinct objective and feasible model.
motivation_note: Martin and Wong equivalence statements are source motivation only; do not infer or prove formulation equivalence from this audit.
priority_note: The curated record’s status open and literature cutoff 2026-08-21 are dated curation, not an authenticated present-day priority theorem.
